name: Parables of Jesus
description: Eight weekly Sunday-school lessons on the stories Jesus told, with a short note and questions for discussion.

days.title: The Sower
days.note: Jesus often taught with everyday pictures. Here a farmer scatters seed on four kinds of ground. The seed is the same each time; what differs is the soil. Jesus explains the story himself, so let his explanation guide the class.
questions: Which of the four soils do you recognise in your own life right now?
What things can choke the word before it grows?
What helps good soil stay good?

days.title: The Good Samaritan
days.note: A lawyer asks, “Who is my neighbour?” Jesus answers with a story where the hero is someone his listeners would not expect. The question turns from “Who deserves my help?” to “Who will I be a neighbour to?”
questions: Why might the priest and the Levite have walked past?
Who are the people we find it hardest to see as neighbours?
What is one practical way to show mercy this week?

days.title: The Lost Sheep and the Lost Coin
days.note: Religious leaders grumble that Jesus welcomes sinners. He replies with two short stories about searching until something lost is found, and about the joy that follows.
questions: What do these stories show about how God sees one person?
Why is there so much joy when the lost is found?
Who might feel “lost” in our church or community?

days.title: The Prodigal Son
days.note: The third story in Luke 15 has two sons and a father who runs. Notice both sons: one leaves home, the other stays home, and both need the father’s grace.
questions: What surprises you about how the father responds?
Do you relate more to the younger son or the older son? Why?
How does this story change how we welcome others back?

days.title: The Mustard Seed and the Yeast
days.note: Two tiny stories with one big idea: God’s kingdom starts small and quietly, but it grows and spreads until it changes everything around it.
questions: Where have you seen something small grow into something big?
Why might God choose to work through small beginnings?
What small act of faith could you take this week?

days.title: The Unforgiving Servant
days.note: Peter asks how many times he must forgive. Jesus tells of a servant forgiven a debt he could never repay, who then refuses to forgive a small one.
questions: Compare the two debts in the story. What is Jesus showing us?
Why can forgiving others be so hard?
How does remembering God’s forgiveness help us forgive?

days.title: The Talents
days.note: A master entrusts his servants with his money while he is away. The story is about faithfulness with what we have been given, whether much or little.
questions: What has God entrusted to you: gifts, time, people, resources?
Why did the third servant hide what he was given?
What would being faithful with a little look like for you?

days.title: The Wise and Foolish Builders
days.note: Jesus ends the Sermon on the Mount with two houses that look the same until the storm comes. The difference is not hearing his words, but doing them.
questions: What storms test the foundations of our lives?
What is the difference between hearing and doing Jesus’ words?
Looking back over these parables, which one do you most want to put into practice?
